This is a visually gorgeous twin-stick shooter with a neat (but gameplay irrelevant) gimmick. Enemies and some other effects cause paint splatters to trail across the stage, in styles and ways that differ from level to level: Maybe they're big fat slab-strokes one map, then tiny pencil lines another, or dabs that 'dye' an invisible pattern already on the canvas. A+ for visuals and sound design, really unique and fun stuff. The actual gameplay is fine, but the more I come back to the game the less I actually enjoy it. The hitboxes are jank and huge, your damage is anemic, item descriptions are worse than Isaac's for no thematic reason, shop prices are way out of whack with income, it's extremely hard to craft a build, Energy items are bad, the Energy regain is worse, and the entire Fame mechanic is inscrutable and feels useless. I feel bad reversing my review here but I just don't have fun when I play Antipaint, as beautiful as it is to look at my works.

AH yes, finally a rogue-like for artists! A pretty simple and fun game with a simple premise and fun concept! I finished the game already and I had a blast while playing! OST is wonderful and really enjoyable and the option of colours and chaos you can create is always fun! I do wish there was some more modes for repeatability which I do have some suggestions for but otherwise I had a really great time playing Antipaint! [h3]Suggestions for additional content and updates:[/h3] - [b]Indecisive[/b] - a game mode where you start the game with a random weapon every round and it changes for each level, weapon upgrades carry over to the next random weapon, in order to unlock it you must get all tools. [i]Some artists have a struggle to choose what they wanna draw, change their style or just simple change their entire self image, this could sometimes slow one down but also could push you the right direction.[/i] - [b]Pain-t Endurance[/b] - a game mode concept where levels progressively get harder and harder and the only way to end a stage is to die. You start only with one health point, and all health upgrades are luxury you have to buy as bonus for your next levels You get more money the longer you last in a level. You can only end your run or die in a boss level. [i]Some artists just refuse to let down, always going out and doing their best! Showing that they can make a change and impress the world with their endurance, as long as they don't make a stumble or its over for them.[/i] - [b]Progressive Artist[/b] - Similar to a regular game mode however stages are filled with tiny action proms and button presses actions you need to perform in stage to raise your fame, the goal of this game mode is simply to raise enough fame before confronting the next boss, if you don't you simply get a instant game over. [i]This game encourages doing more things and extra as a artist to impress your audience while drawing in order to make a impression to deserve to progress as artist in your art carrier.[/i] I hope this feedback helps you to inspire to add more additional content I seriously would enjoy more variety in gameplay. I absolutely recommend antipaint.

Antipaint, developed and published by Vilius Prakapas, is a vibrant and inventive roguelite shooter that transforms chaotic combat into living, abstract artwork. At first glance, it appears to be a colorful top-down action game in the tradition of arena-based survival shooters, but it quickly distinguishes itself through its central artistic mechanic. Every enemy you defeat, every dash you make, and every chaotic encounter you survive leaves behind splashes and streaks of paint, gradually turning each level into a unique visual composition. What emerges is not just a cleared battlefield, but a canvas shaped by your performance. The core gameplay revolves around tight, fast-paced arena combat. You control a small painter armed with artistic tools repurposed as weapons—brushes, rollers, sprays, and other creative implements used to dispatch waves of surreal, paint-themed enemies. The movement is responsive and fluid, with dodging playing a crucial role in survival. Combat demands constant repositioning, quick reactions, and careful crowd management as enemies swarm from multiple directions. Despite its accessible control scheme, the difficulty ramps up steadily, pushing players to master both offense and evasion. Where Antipaint truly stands apart is in how it visually tracks your journey. Each arena begins as a relatively blank space, and as enemies burst into color upon defeat, the floor fills with dynamic splatters and trails. The patterns created are not predesigned textures but the result of your movements and tactical decisions. If you kite enemies in circular motions, spirals of paint form across the floor. If you carve straight paths through dense swarms, bold streaks slash across the canvas. Every completed stage becomes a visual artifact of that particular run—an accidental painting born of strategy and chaos. The roguelite structure ensures strong replay value. Enemy compositions, item drops, and environmental elements shift between runs, keeping encounters unpredictable. Players collect various upgrades that alter weapon behavior, improve survivability, or introduce entirely new mechanics. Some items amplify damage output, others modify movement or add reactive effects, encouraging experimentation. The synergy between upgrades can dramatically alter playstyle, turning a cautious, evasive build into an aggressive paint-spreading frenzy or vice versa. This layered progression reinforces the “just one more run” loop that defines successful roguelites. Unlockable characters further deepen the experience. Each new character offers distinct starting abilities or stat distributions, subtly reshaping how runs unfold. While the core combat remains consistent, these variations introduce strategic diversity. The combination of character traits and randomized items creates a broad range of possible builds, ensuring that mastery requires adaptability rather than repetition. The visual presentation is bold and kinetic. The aesthetic leans toward retro-inspired pixel art, but the explosion of color during combat gives it a contemporary flair. Neon splashes and vibrant contrasts create a spectacle that grows more intense as the battlefield fills. Despite the chaos, the design maintains clarity, ensuring players can still track enemy movements and avoid incoming damage. The art direction balances beauty and functionality, allowing the evolving canvas to serve both as decoration and readable gameplay space. Sound design complements the visual energy. Combat effects emphasize impact and motion, while the soundtrack underscores the frantic pace of survival. The audio reinforces the rhythm of gameplay without overwhelming it, maintaining immersion during prolonged sessions. Together with the visuals, it creates a cohesive sensory experience that feels both energetic and creatively expressive. One of the game’s most compelling qualities is how it reframes success. Completion is not only about defeating waves or clearing stages, but about observing the artwork you have unintentionally created. The aftermath of each level serves as a moment of reflection, where chaos resolves into composition. This mechanic adds emotional resonance to victory, transforming the battlefield into a gallery of spontaneous, abstract pieces. It subtly rewards not only skill but style. While Antipaint excels in creativity and replayability, its arena-focused design means the gameplay loop remains centered on combat. Players seeking deep narrative arcs or extensive environmental storytelling may find it minimalist in that regard. However, the emphasis on mechanics and emergent art ensures that the experience rarely feels stale. Its simplicity is offset by build diversity and the ever-changing visual outcome of each run. Ultimately, Antipaint succeeds by fusing action and artistry into a cohesive whole. It is both a skill-driven roguelite and a generative art experiment, where every battle paints a story in color. Vilius Prakapas has crafted a game that feels joyful, chaotic, and refreshingly original within the crowded roguelite genre. For players who appreciate tight arena combat and creative visual feedback, Antipaint offers an experience that is as satisfying to watch as it is to play. Rating: 9/10

当你想要成为世界上最厉害的画家时，但你所创作的画又怪异又抽象，在自己眼里根本称不上艺术（抽象派不好吗），而人类已经有了那么多伟大的画作，仔细想想自己根本无法比拟，但如果这些伟大的画作通通消失了，自己的画岂不就成为了世界上最伟大的画作，抱着这样的心理，玩家所操控的“艺术家”踏上了消灭所有画作的旅程…… [h2] 简单易上手 [/h2] 在《美术危机》中，玩家将在一块块不同样式的画布上与各种颜料战斗，将它们击败会在画布上留下各种颜色，从而提高自己的名望，创作出一幅幅奇异的画作保留在画廊之中。玩家能在开始游戏前选择颜料盘作为这次画作的主要颜色，接下来选择人物和武器作为本次作画的艺术家，不同人物初始有着不同属性和能力，武器有着不同攻击方式，它们会在局内达成条件后逐渐解锁，从而可以创作颜色更加丰富艳丽的画作，组合成多样的战斗玩法。 局内战斗就是在一块有限空间的画布上面对四面八方涌来的多样颜料敌人，在首轮结束后会进入道具房间选择道具，第二轮结束会前往商店，在商店可花费金钱购买道具、买饮料、升级武器、用奖券抽奖、“以物易物”之类的，当然游戏也有着一些隐藏要素在道具房和商店，它们通常都非常明显这就要靠玩家自己探索了。 而在经历几次道具和商店后就能挑战游戏非常有特色的BOSS了，所有BOSS都是比较知名的画作进行了比较抽象的改版，什么古埃及壁画、拿破仑翻越阿尔卑斯山、蒙娜丽莎等等，不过虽然BOSS都有一些机制，但挑战起来没什么难度，唯一要注意的是所有BOSS都是躺着的纸片人，整个身体都是实体，触碰体积较大，稍微擦个边都可能会受伤。 [h2] 总结 [/h2] 总体来说，《美术危机》的创意十分有趣，各种搞怪的名画BOSS为游玩时带来了有趣的体验，但相反游戏重复可玩性其实并不高，不同角色、武器之间的差异并不大，角色也只是数值、属性以及携带的道具不同，稍微有些变化的武器在局内也没有太丰富的构筑体验，但对于喜欢这种轻松的肉鸽游戏的玩家来说，十分推荐入手尝试，体验一下不怎么需要脑子的创作乐趣。 [quote]漫话漫谈，期待关注:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/44551694/]写生漫话家[/url] ←节约宝贵时间，阅读省流测评~ 欢迎加入漫话家的大家庭:[url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/14030826]写生漫话家[/url]←共同探讨游戏中的精彩片段，向玩家展现第九艺术的魅力~

[h1]变相成为画家——《美术危机》[/h1] 犹记得儿时的梦想，成为达芬奇一样的画家，那知道只学了一半，成了一半达芬奇，达芬半。但是，在《美术危机》里，我找到了成为达芬奇的秘密！ [h2]自由作画！[/h2] 在游戏中，我们所扮演的是一只画笔，通过攻击画布上的道具，来激发各种各样的灵感，生成不一样的作品。 每当通过关卡后，可以在道具中进行3选1，获得额外加成。 比如：经济压力——没钱加攻速 高塔——加攻速减移速 美味樱桃——额外获得生命 前面都很普通，但是道具分为普通、稀有、直到传说，你们看这传说道具，牛不牛逼！ 同时，每一大关卡中，可以获得画笔加成、转转盘、商店等一系列额外增益。 当前面小怪打完后，将会面对传说的画作。什么飞翔的路德、笨瓜艺术、愤怒的法国人，哈哈哈，都非常搞笑。路德可以分成无数个小头、笨瓜可以召唤一堆黄瓜。法国人尽然会召唤一堆马，而且移速巨快，跑都跑不及。 随着每局游戏获胜或者失败，玩家都将会解锁更多调色板，画笔及武器，最高可达八种武器、十余种角色、直至四十多种配色及百余种搭配。让你把挡在你面前的所谓“经典”通通打倒，你才是唯一真神！ 说实话，其实《美术危机》是将画画与肉鸽相结合的一款游戏，玩家在打败敌人的同时，不断升级自己的效果，再通过不断击败敌人，来收集更多素材，解锁更多绘画。题材非常新颖，游戏中很多名画的梗也非常好玩，整体体验非常的轻松愉快。 希望肉鸽和画画类的玩家值得一试！ [quote]欢迎关注『 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45525570/] 桃你欢心 [/url]』 [b] 桃影扶风评百戏，落墨如歌写人间[/b][/quote]

[h1]为寂寞的夜空画上一个月亮，在打怪中作画[/h1] 类幸存者游戏很多，但像《美术危机》这般在战斗之余还带点艺术气息的确是独一份的存在。 本作脑洞大开般的将画布布置成了战斗场景，而不同的画笔则是你的武器。敌人在阵亡后会爆浆，洒出的颜料就化为了五彩斑斓的画作。 你是在打怪吗？不，你是在创作艺术！“为寂寞的夜空画上一个月亮，画上有你能用手触到的彩虹，画中有我决定不灭的星空。”甚至于游戏中的BOSS，都是各式各样你熟悉的但是又经过变种的世界名画，这何尝不是另一种形式的暴力美学呢？ 具体来说说游戏的战斗模式，从本质上来讲它依然是类幸存者游戏那一套，刷完一张图的怪后进入商店，再进入下一张图，直至打BOSS。玩家可以自我选择是否开启自动瞄准和自动射击。虽然手动模式可以更加精准的进行操控，但是个人建议还是开启自动模式，因为玩这种游戏不就是图个无脑省心吗？ 但是由于武器是画笔，这种挥舞战斗的手感还是挺奇特的。而且如果你在短时间内一次性消灭了大量敌人，还会进入所谓的“灵感爆发”状态，画布两侧会有泉涌特效，玩家也会有一个移速和射速的实质加成。 而在关卡中途的商店环节，我们也可以升级画刷，购买各种增益道具。进入的彩虹关卡还有一个类似于接金币的环节，还是挺有意思的。此外如果你无伤过一关，还可以开启潜能，相应也会出现更好品质的道具。 总的来说，本作玩法中规中矩，但最有特色的一点无疑是其独有的艺术气息。战斗本身像画画，打的越好，画作的数量和质量也越高，这种奇怪的正反馈也是绝了。 [quote]关注「 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/42276832//]鸿源鉴游组」 [/url] [/quote] [u][b] 会当逢佳游，始可见鸿源。 [/b][/u]

You know how some people say the best way to win by default is to take out the competition? Well this is how this game handles that as a mediocre artist wanting to become popular. You murder all sorts of paint blobs and artworks with artistic tools and make works of art that look like you splattered colors in an attempt to get through your art block. Its a decent rougelite shooter with a creative outlook into the art world and shows that you really need to work at something to make it somewhere, and in this case, its proving you have talent in painting, albeit in a roundabout way. The game offers a lot of variety with its choices and offers a strong challenge if you feel like it. It may have some flaws but overall, it isn't so bad to unleash your inner artist.
